ceramic.title: Testimonials | FIBACT
ceramic.snippet: I was an employee of Erstwhile VMware (now Broadcom) in Bengaluru, India. Broadcom announced the acquisition of VMware in May 2022 and the transaction completed in Nov 2023. The transaction was roughly split at 50-50% cash/equity. Being an employee of VMware, holding stocks of VMW (RSUs), I was entitled for any payout that happened as part of the acquisition transaction.During the course of the months leading up to the completion of the transaction, we did not have full clarity on the payout from our stocks and its tax treatment. The FAQs mostly mentioned that we should consult our tax advisors. Most of us held onto our stocks with the hope for a good future under AVGO (Broadcom stock ticker symbol). Upon completion of the transaction, when we received our payout, we were taken aback that a substantial amount (25% of the payout) was withheld as tax by the stockbroker (ETRADE). This was not a case with a few of us - it was common across all employees. The reason being, the entire payout was (mis)characterized as dividend (subject to DTAA tax withholding), and not as sale of stock (subject to capital gains tax falling under individual purview).Being non-US people, we had no clue as to how to go about this problem and get our money back. We initially tried reaching out to the stockbroker and our own company's stock administration teams to try and get the issue sorted out. Months dragged with no results. Eventually, we had to individually figure out this for ourselves.Believing in the power of collective approach, a few of us formed a group and sought advice from CPA firms - we started this around Feb-Mar 2024. At first, we were in a learning mode ourselves, trying to get a high-level overview of the US tax laws and how a non-US person would go about asking for a refund from IRS. Some CPA firms proved hard to work with, were not approachable, scaring us that even email correspondences beyond the first email would be billable by the hour.

Chip developer Broadcom Inc., with deep roots in Irvine, has been on a roll since April as its share price more than doubled and its market cap neared $2 trillion.

  “2025 was another strong year for Broadcom, and we see the spending momentum by our customers for AI continuing to accelerate in 2026,” Chief Executive Hock Tan told analysts on a conference call.

  Harsh Kumar, senior research analyst at Piper Sandler & Co., was upbeat about Broadcom in a note to clients dated Dec. 11, the day the results were released.

  “AVGO continues to be on a roll, delivering blockbuster results and guide,” Kumar wrote, referring to the company by its stock ticker symbol.

  Palo Alto-based Broadcom spent more than two decades in Irvine before decamping and eventually settling in Silicon Valley in 2018. Company co-founder and chairman Henry Samueli is a major OC philanthropist and real estate tycoon.

  Broadcom still maintains a large presence in Irvine. It easily retained its No. 1 spot on this year’s Business Journal list of largest semiconductor firms by headcount, keeping its local number at 1,300. Its workforce in Irvine includes software managers and semiconductor engineers.

  Broadcom is positioned to control up to 80% of the custom AI chip market known as tensor processing units, or TPUs, Daniel Newman, chief executive of Futurum analyst firm, told the Wall Street Journal last week.

  Broadcom’s Tan confirmed to analysts that the company’s AI business has lower gross margins than other units and hence as it grows in importance, the companywide gross margin may come down.

  For fiscal 2025, Broadcom’s sales climbed 24% to $63.9 billion, and its adjusted profit soared 35% to $43 billion. Its cash flow was $26.9 billion.

A  ticker symbol or  stock symbol is an abbreviation used to uniquely identify publicly traded shares of a particular publicly listed company or security on a particular stock exchange . Ticker symbols are arrangements of symbols or characters (generally Latin letters or digits) which provide a shorthand for investors to refer to, purchase, and research securities. Some exchanges include ticker extensions, which encode additional information such as share class, bankruptcy status, or voting rights into the ticker. 1
